where: Section 2, oblique resolution (the sentence "The angle opposite F is the angle between the two chosen lines")
problem: The two statements about P and Q are correct, but the third is geometrically wrong. In the force triangle OAC (OA = P along line a, AC = Q parallel to line b, OC = F), the interior angle opposite F is the angle at A between AO (opposite to line a) and AC (along line b), which is 180° − α, not α. A student who draws the triangle will measure 105° for the 0°/75° case and think the text is wrong. The numbers still come out right only because sin(180° − α) = sin α.
fix: Write: "The angle opposite F is 180° − α, where α is the angle between the two chosen lines. Its sine equals sin α, so the sine rule is written F / sin α." Then in the worked example, step 5 should read: "F = 50 N is opposite 180° − 75° = 105°, and sin 105° = sin 75° = 0.9659."
